{{Wireless adapter |brand=Samsung |model=SWL-2000P |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=11/23/1999 |manuf_country= |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |if=PCI |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |fcc_id=E2XSWL-2000P |ic_id= |chip1_brand=Harris |chip1_model=HFA3841 |chip2_brand=Harris |chip2_model= |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |flags= |ant_conn=unknown |802dot11_protocols=b |txchains= |rxchains= |sstreams= |oui=00:02:78 |lin_driver= |win_driver=[http://web.archive.org/web/20010616114042/http://www.magiclan.com/common/download.jsp?filelocation=/cont01/w3sem/upload/support/jsp_4856.dat&content_type=application/octet-stream&filename=ml11_v311.exe here (via archive.org)] }} "SAMSUNG", "11M PCI WLAN", and "REV : C9907" is silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos.
While the device is shown with a '''Lucent''' branded MAC in the FCC photos, this device appears to be PRISM based.
The Windows PCMCIA device string for this product is presumed to be... *PCMCIA\SAMSUNG-11Mbps_WLAN_PCI_Card-BD65 **'''SAMSUNG 11Mbps Wireless LAN PCI Card'''
The device uses a '''Cirrus Logic''' / '''Basis Communications''' CL-PD6729-QC-E PCI->PCMCIA host adapter.
[http://www.monkey.org/openbsd/archive/misc/0111/msg01048.html '''Wavelan SAMSUNG SWL-2000P''' on an openbsd mailing list from 2001] :00:02:78 OUI ('''Samsung''')
